findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the positive rationale for making all eight tombstones `error`-class (vs the registry's established `warn` treatment for inert value-preserving renames like REBAR_PUSH), or classify the six inert renames as `warn` and reserve `error` for the two semantic/unsafe aliases (REBAR_NO_SYNC, REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE).
evidence: Plan Approach: 'Replace each `_permanent` row with an `_tomb` entry at `error` behavior'
Plan Context: 'Because `REBAR_NO_SYNC` changes pull semantics and `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE` controls an unsafe bypass, silent fallback is unsafe.' — cites only two of eight

Existing registry convention: `_tomb("env", "REBAR_PUSH", "REBAR_SYNC_PUSH", "warn")` — inert renames are warn-class, while semantic/load-bearing ones (TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR, REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE) are error-class
findings.finding: The plan mandates uniform `error`-behavior tombstones for all eight aliases, but the existing tombstone registry deliberately splits `error` (load-bearing/semantic-changing, e.g. TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR, REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE) from `warn` (inert value-preserving renames, e.g. REBAR_PUSH->REBAR_SYNC_PUSH). Six of the eight (COMPACT_THRESHOLD, SCRATCH_BASE_DIR, REBAR_ACLI_TIMEOUT, RECONCILER_ABSENT_GET_BUDGET, REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED, verify.overlap_enabled) are inert renames matching the warn-class precedent. The plan's own safety rationale ('silent fallback is unsafe') only names REBAR_NO_SYNC and REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE, yet it applies `error` to all eight without stating why the inert renames also warrant fail-loud rather than the codebase's established warn-class treatment for inert renames.
findings.location: Approach ('replace each `_permanent` row with an `_tomb` entry at `error` behavior'); Context/Problem (safety rationale names only REBAR_NO_SYNC and REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE)
scenarios: An operator with only COMPACT_THRESHOLD set (a purely ergonomic value-preserving rename) has their whole config load aborted via RemovedInputError rather than warned+migrated, diverging from the REBAR_PUSH precedent
